_meta.note: Curated strategy layer (English). Translated/summarized from the Russian-language channel t.me/kiritastrich with aoe2database.com as secondary context. Exact civ numbers/bonuses live in each civ's auto-derived 'facts' block; this file is qualitative application only. No invented precise timestamps. Edited freely; never overwritten by upstream refresh (rule R5).

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated Fast Castle (~20–22 vills), then Stable + Blacksmith, mass ~4 Scout Cavalry + Scorpions with a couple of Monks. Best on resource-rich maps: 2+ boar, 8 sheep, 3–4 deer.

buildOrders.title: Full Feudal + Market age-up
buildOrders.detail: Play full Feudal with a Market and buy the age advance; the gold-mining bonus funds a large gold pool for gold units.

turks.buildNote: Top pick for the scouts+scorps build: the Scout-line auto-upgrades + free Light Cavalry armor make the 4-Scout spam essentially free to tech, and faster gold funds Scorpions + Monks. Clean gunpowder transition (Chemistry is free; gunpowder techs −50%).
recommendations: Abuse the free Scout upgrades and faster gold — go heavy on Scorpions with a few Monks for conversion/heal.
Transition into Hand Cannoneers + Bombard Cannons in Imperial (free Chemistry, cheap gunpowder techs).
Do NOT rely on trash: you have no Elite Skirmisher and no Halberdier.
strengths: Free Chemistry; gunpowder techs −50%; gunpowder +25% HP
Free Scout-line upgrades + Light Cavalry armor
weaknesses: Weak trash line (no Elite Skirmisher, no Halberdier, no Onager)
No Siege Engineers; monks lack Illumination/Heresy

timings.label: Fast Castle
timings.detail: Click Castle Age ~20–22 vills → Stable + Blacksmith

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Same accelerated FC frame as Turks (~20–22 vills → Stable + Blacksmith → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks). On resource-rich maps.

celts.buildNote: Like Burmese with auto woodcutting — you barely feel the missing barding/saddle, because the woodcutting bonus funds the siege mass. Strongest siege in the game for this comp; the cost is weak Monks.
recommendations: Lean on Scorpions — your siege fires faster and the woodcutting bonus pays for the mass.
Keep Monks minimal (weak monastery); use them only for spot-heals/conversions.
Mobile infantry + fast siege lets you reposition before the opponent stabilizes.
weaknesses: Weak Monks (no Redemption/Heresy/etc. options as strong)

timings.label: Fast Castle
timings.detail: Click Castle ~20–22 vills → siege workshop fast via wood bonus

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → Stable + Blacksmith → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. Cavaliers/Knights are the natural follow-up.

franks.buildNote: Scouts are slightly weaker than Turks' baseline, but the free cavalry HP (bloodlines-style) adds weight for push strats, faster berries smooth the FC, and you skip farm-size upgrades. Decent Scorpions; the cost is trash Monks (good only for converting answer-knights).
recommendations: Use the cavalry HP bonus to win scout/knight fights and push with confidence.
Transition into Knights/Cavaliers — your stable is the strongest part of the tree.
Don't invest in Monks beyond emergency knight conversions.
strengths: Cavalry +20% HP from Feudal; auto Bloodlines
Faster foraging; no farm-size upgrades needed
weaknesses: Thin archer/siege options vs heavy ranged

timings.label: Fast Castle
timings.detail: Smooth FC off faster berries → Stable push

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. The hunter bonus makes deer/boar maps especially fast.

mongols.buildNote: A strong analog to Franks; the cavalry HP kicks in from Castle Age, Scorpions are fine, and Monks are a bit stronger than Franks/Celts. The hunter bonus can make the FC noticeably earlier.
recommendations: Use the hunter bonus to hit a faster up-time on deer/boar maps.
Pair the scout/scorpion spike with Mangudai or Light Cav in late Castle/Imperial.
Mobile siege repositions quickly thanks to the siege movement bonus.
strengths: Hunters +40% → very fast FC on animal-heavy maps
weaknesses: No economy bonus on closed/resource-poor maps

timings.label: Fast Castle
timings.detail: Earlier up-time off the hunter (+40%) bonus; the source channel hit a no-idle 17+2 — click Castle at ~18 pop — as a benchmark.

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. Hunted/livestock food doesn't decay, so you bank more food for the age-up and unit spam.

jurchens.buildNote: The no-decay food bonus gives a real resource edge, and +25% attack speed on mounted units makes the scouts hit harder. Main weakness: Monks.
recommendations: Bank the no-decay food into a faster age-up and a bigger scout/scorpion mass.
Use the mounted-unit attack-speed bonus on scouts and (later) cavalry archers/fire lancers.
Cheap/fast siege & fortification upgrades (Castle Age Siege Engineers) help the push.
strengths: Food doesn't decay (hunted/livestock) → more banked food
Siege/fort upgrades cheap & fast; Castle-Age Siege Engineers
weaknesses: Reliant on hunting/livestock for the food edge

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. Stable-unit discount makes the scout spam cheaper and lets you mix Knights.

berbers.buildNote: Stable-unit cost discount makes the scout spam cheaper, Knights move faster, and Monks are decent — so this is one of the most flexible variations of the build.
recommendations: Spam scouts/knights off the stable discount; mix Genitours vs archer civs.
Faster villagers/knights let you dictate engagements and raids.
Decent Monks → you can actually convert/heal, unlike Franks/Celts.
strengths: Stable units cheaper → cheap scout/knight spam
weaknesses: Fewer eco bonuses outside unit cost

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. Sits between Turks and Celts: a wood discount + extra gold fund the siege and the monks.

buildOrders.title: Full Feudal + Market age-up
buildOrders.detail: Full Feudal with a Market; buy the age advance off the gold economy.

malians.buildNote: A middle ground between Turks and Celts — wood discount pays for siege, extra gold pays for monks and gunpowder, and the monastery is actually decent. Very flexible.
recommendations: Use the wood discount to mass Scorpions/towers cheaply.
Extra gold → mix Monks and, later, gunpowder (Gbetos, BBC).
Farimba (+5 infantry attack) makes a late infantry switch devastating.
strengths: Decent Monks; strong infantry with Farimba
weaknesses: Siege capped (no Siege Ram elite options in some lines)

timings.label: Fast Castle
timings.detail: Wood+gold economy → smooth FC into scorps+monks

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. Extra food from herdables and a strong ram option complement the comp.

gurjaras.buildNote: Extra food from sheep (you can herd them out) plus a very strong ram to complement scorpions + scouts, and decent Monks. The siege ram follow-up is the differentiator.
recommendations: Bank herdable food for a faster/cheaper age-up.
Pair Scorpions with the strong rams for a hard push.
Use Shrivamsha Riders to absorb archer fire in front of the siege.
strengths: Strong siege ram to pair with scorpions

timings.label: Fast Castle
timings.detail: Herdable food → smooth FC; ram+scorpion push

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. Stream-tested and confirmed to fit the fast-FC frame very well.

lithuanians.buildNote: Fits the fast FC cleanly. Early relics stack attack onto the knight line, so the natural follow-up (Knights/Cavaliers) hits extremely hard.
recommendations: Grab relics early — each adds +1 attack to your knight line.
Follow the scout/scorpion spike with a relic-boosted Knight mass.
Monks are usable for relic collection and conversions.
lithuanians.strengths: Relic-stacked knight attack; smooth fast Castle; decent Monks

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. Played for this build in tournament.
buildOrders.map: Vale de Selva and similar resource-rich maps

burmese.buildNote: Played for this build in tournament. Auto woodcutting-style economy and free lumber-camp upgrades smooth the FC, and strong Monks cover the build's usual weak spot.
recommendations: Lean on the strong Monks (cheap monastery techs) — they patch the comp's usual monk weakness.
Use the infantry attack-per-age bonus for a late infantry switch (Arambai).
Free lumber-camp upgrades keep the siege mass affordable.

timings.label: Fast Castle
timings.detail: Smooth FC; strong-monk variation of the build

buildOrders.title: Fast Castle → 4 Scouts + Scorpions (+ Monks)
buildOrders.detail: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vills) → 4 Scouts + Scorpions + Monks. Played for this build in tournament; no building prerequisites make the build very flexible.

khmer.buildNote: Played in tournament for this build. No building prerequisites and drop-off-anywhere farms/vills make the FC and transitions unusually smooth; Battle Elephants are the power follow-up.
recommendations: Exploit no-prerequisite buildings to drop the siege workshop / stable instantly.
Follow the spike with Battle Elephants for a hard power transition.
Villagers drop resources anywhere — less walking, smoother eco.
strengths: Villagers drop off anywhere; fast houses

buildOrders.title: Full Feudal gold-unit play
buildOrders.detail: Go full Feudal with strong gold units (Eagle/Archer line) + the attack upgrade; pair with Monks. Conceptually similar to prioritizing gold mining first.

aztecs.buildNote: All your strong units cost gold, so a full-feudal gold-unit + monk style fits. The +50 gold start and faster military production smooth it.
recommendations: Open full-feudal with Archers/Eagles + Monks; grab the attack upgrade early.
Use the +50 gold start for an instant Barracks/Archery edge.
Monks are top-tier — convert and heal aggressively.
weaknesses: Reliant on gold and monk micro

buildOrders.title: Full Feudal gold-unit play
buildOrders.detail: Full Feudal with the cheap archer line + monks. Resources last longer, sustaining the gold-unit mass.

maya.buildNote: Like Aztecs, your strong units are gold-based; full-feudal archers + monks fits. The 'resources last +15%' bonus extends your gold/food, suiting a sustained gold-unit style.
recommendations: Mass Archers/Plumes in Feudal/Castle; the resource bonus sustains production.
Use cheaper walls to protect while you macro.
Pair with Monks where the tree allows.

timings.label: Full Feudal
timings.detail: Sustained archer/monk mass off lasting resources

buildOrders.title: 23-pop Militia full Feudal (Vinch-style)
buildOrders.detail: A ~23-pop Militia/drush-into-full-feudal build; by then normalize food income. Needs permanent walling to survive fast aggression.

inca.buildNote: Conceptually suited to full-feudal American-civ play (e.g. the 23-pop militia build). The catch in AoE2 is game speed/early aggression, so walling is mandatory. The source channel rates Incas highly — its full guide is titled 'You don't realize how strong the Incas are' and it opens its civ tier list with them.
recommendations: Open with early Militia pressure, then stabilize food and go full feudal.
Wall aggressively — you need time vs faster/aggressive civs.
Villagers benefit from blacksmith upgrades; Kamayuks anchor mid-game.
Lean on the underrated core — blacksmith-upgraded villagers + Kamayuks + Andean Slingers (anti-archer) is the payoff the source channel highlights.
May 2026 patch (kiritastrich): unit food discount changed to 15/20/25/30% by age (except Kamayuk); cheaper Slingers (50f/25w) and reworked Champs make the infantry + Slinger core far stronger.
weaknesses: Slow vs early aggression without walling

buildOrders.title: Full Feudal idea (American civs)
buildOrders.detail: Conceptual fit for full-feudal play alongside Inca/Tupi/Muisca; needs walling vs early aggression. Bonuses: see facts block.

recommendations: Consider a full-feudal style; wall to buy time vs aggressive civs.

buildOrders.title: Full Feudal + Market age-up
buildOrders.detail: Full Feudal with a Market; buy the age advance. The gold economy supports the gold-unit/monk play.

armenians.buildNote: Listed for the market-based full-feudal age-up style. Mule-Cart economy and early age access to Militia/Spear upgrades enable flexible feudal pressure.
recommendations: Use Mule Carts for a compact, raid-resistant economy.
Abuse earlier-age infantry upgrades for feudal pressure.
Composite Bowmen + Warrior Priests give a strong castle-age core.
May 2026 patch (kiritastrich): Mule-Cart gather bonus raised 40%→45% — faster wood/gold/stone, a solid eco buff.
strengths: Mule Cart economy; earlier infantry upgrades
Strong unique units (Composite Bowman, Warrior Priest)
weaknesses: Reliant on gold for the unique core

buildOrders.title: Market-based play (different market rules)
buildOrders.detail: Treated separately because the Market works differently (much better rates/cheap fees) — enables market-heavy age-ups and resource swaps other civs can't do.

saracens.buildNote: The market advantage is the defining lever: cheap, efficient trading/buying lets you force age-ups or rebalance resources in ways other civs can't. Build around the market, not a fixed BO.
recommendations: Use the market aggressively to force age-ups and rebalance food/gold.
Mamelukes + Archers form a strong mobile core once stable.
Galley-line bonuses make this a top water civ.
weaknesses: No real early eco bonus outside the market
Bonus depends on active market use

timings.label: Market age-up
timings.detail: Buy resources to force age transitions

buildOrders.title: Cheap age-up + Flemish Militia + Archers
buildOrders.detail: Flemish Revolution + Archers is pricey, but Burgundians get a cheaper age-up, making the timing viable. Economy upgrades arrive an age early.

burgundians.buildNote: Flemish Militia + archers is an expensive combo, but the cheap age-up and early-arriving eco upgrades (e.g. early Wheelbarrow/Crop Rotation tier) make the spike affordable.
recommendations: Use the cheap age-up to hit key timings earlier than opponents.
Pair Flemish Militia with archers for a mixed-feudal/castle spike.
Relic gold and early eco techs fund the expensive unit mix.
May 2026 patch (kiritastrich): food-tech discount raised 33%→40%, pushing the civ toward Arabia viability.
strengths: Cheaper age-ups; eco upgrades an age early
weaknesses: Flemish + archer mix is gold/food heavy

timings.label: Cheap age-up
timings.detail: Earlier age transitions fund the expensive unit mix
